στοῖχος , ὁ, (στείχω, cf. στίχος)
A.row in an ascending series, ὁ πρῶτος ς. τῶν ἀναβαθμῶν the first course of (masonry composing) the steps, Hdt. 2.125 ; course of bricks, etc., in building, IG 22.463.58 , 1682.10 ; esp. file of persons marching one behind another, as in a procession, ἐπὶ στοίχου,= στοιχηδόν, Ar. Ec. 756 ; “νῆσοι κατὰ στοῖχον κείμεναι”
Th. 2.102
; “κατὰ στοίχους”
Ar. Fr. 79
; of ships, column, “ἐν στοίχοις τρισί”
A. Pers. 366
; of soldiers, file, Th. 4.47 ; “διὰ στοίχων ὁπλῖται παρατεταγμένοι”
D.C. 63.4
; of deer swimming, Opp. C. 2.226 ; of the files (opp. ζυγόν VIII) of the chorus in plays, Poll. 4.108 , 109 ; row of columns, IG 22.1668.12 ; of factors, Arist. Metaph. 1092b34 ; of verses, “ἔπη . . ἀλλότρια τοῦ ς. τῆς ποιήσεως”
Afric. Cest.Oxy. 412.51
.
II. a line of poles supporting hunting-nets, into which the game were driven, X. Cyn. 6.10 , 21 .
III. τοῦ ς. καταλαβόντος τὴν ἡμετέραν βουλήν since the turn has come to our senate,
POxy. 1119.12
(iii A.D.).
From A Greek-English Lexicon (Henry George Liddell, Robert Scott, Oxford, Clarendon Press, 1940)
